# Chapter Eleven: The Order

Vic entered the room where the two priests sat with coffee and pastries, “I see you’re finally up young man” said Bishop Talbot, giving Sam a knowing look. Sam just shook his head and continued to sip on his coffee, he didn’t like the older man’s methods but he had to agree they seem to be working. Vic had been in there with the weapons for hours surely he must have touched them and seen the visions. Sam wasn’t sure what he would have seen as every hunter was different and every vision meant for that moment to further them as a hunter. So who knows what visions and what hunter Vic would have been studying for these many hours.

Sam knew from studying many hunters over the years that it was not random whatever power governed the weapons and the visions chose them based on the person and the need. IT would show Vic someone he could identify with and then teach him what he needed to know.

Vic came in and sat down on the far couch, grabbing a pastry with a little grunt of pain. Trying to stifle it as not to show too much weakness, he didn’t know why but for some reason he did not trust the older priest, the guy rubbed him the wrong way. But Sam he had known, he might have gotten older but he was still the same Sam he remembered as a young man and that was the only reason Vic had not bolted yet.

“So someone want to explain the little toys that were left for me” he asked munching on a pastry.

The bishop leaned back and folded his hands, “what did you see Vic” he asked casually but Sam could see the interest in his eyes. Vic thought about it for a second and then saw no harm in telling them, after all he left crazy back about 10 miles after learning about fucking werewolves roaming the country. “I was reliving the memories of some young man named Alfonso, I went through his first hunt and his sword training” he said casually while still munching on the pastry. The Bishop shot a glance at Sam and with a knowing glance nodded to him. Alfonso, of all the people he could have seen, it was Alfonso Sam thought, this was not a coincidence, he and the Bishop would talk about it when Vic wasn’t around. “Anything else” Sam asked leaning forward, did you glean anything from this experience.

Vic nodded noncommittally “A few things, some odd words mostly” he said looking at the Bishop and ignoring Sam’s gaze, something about this man Vic thought, he was up to something and Vic wanted to know what. “Which words Vic” the Bishop asked Vic thought and then shrugged again, no point in hiding it, he wanted to play his cards close to the vest, but he could see the answer was important to the man and it might tip the old priests hand with what he said next Vic looked closely at the old priest and said “Bakhzataa” repeating the Aramaic word for sight. There was a flicker of recognition in the old man’s gaze, just for a second but Vic had caught it. And then the oddest thing happened, the old man seemed to be shrouded in red, in fact he could see heat blooms through the door of the guards outside and one over Sam as well. He leaned back looking around and seeing people on the floor below, there profiles coming through as red blooms of color as they moved around. He gasped repeating the word and the heat blooms vanishing. He did not expect the word to work, though now thinking about it, why not it had worked for Alfonso why wouldn’t it work for him. Maybe it was tied to the weapons he thought. Glancing at Bishop Talbot again “It worked didn’t it Vic, you saw the heat signature of those in the building” he said as if confirming to himself. Vic cocked his head, “How did you know” he asked the old man. Bishop Talbot settled into his chair, I am going to tell you a story, that will enlighten a few things for you.

The Bishop settled back and began to recite the tale

“on July 9th 1572 19 Catholic Priests were put to death, it was said to have been done by a protestant duke who hated Catholics, they were tortured and then shipped to the Netherlands to be executed. The Jesuits wanting to know more about this sent a small contingent of priests to investigate, in the course of their investigations they discovered this duke was an alpha in a pack of werewolves, several of the priests were turned or killed before they caught on to what was happening and of the 10 sent only 3 returned, with an amazing tale to tell. Soon after an order of Jesuits were founded to combat this threat and soldiers with experience with game hunting were recruited, all from royal lines of the time. A priest of the order who had knowledge of certain rites that at the time were considered heresy was consulted and the 12 knights who made up the original hunters of the order were given sacred weapons and ordained gifts from god himself according to the texts. These included the 5 words used by Jesus himself to offer strength, speed, sight, knowledge and of course fire.

The weapons the knights were granted had special abilities, each set was unique. The set you were given access to was from your direct descendant who was one of the original volunteers, when he passed the set was given to Ferdinand the III, in fact he was ordained holding that very sword. They have a replica at the Basilica of course, they could never be allowed the real weapon. Of the original 12 lines only 4 are left, the rest have been destroyed over the centuries by the wolves wanting to stomp out the hunters and their weapons.

This was what you and your family found yourselves in the middle of the other night. You see, because of this you and your children are now targets they will not stop coming after you until you are dead. For this reason, you cannot be allowed to leave the church so you and your family will reside under the churches protection to ensure your safety. This will allow the lineage to continue, we can’t let this line die as we have so few left.” The Bishop finished and leaned back in the chair to let Vic digest this. “So you are saying we are now prisoners of the catholic church?” he asked, with heat in his words. The bishop shook his head “No my boy, just under our complete protection, that is all” Vic didn’t like the sound of that, it sounded more like they were now involuntary wards of this sect. Vic looked around the room and saw the two guards enter. Probably called by some electronic means by the bishop. One remained by the door and the other approached. “You will be sent separately to a location as will your family, your children will be split up better protect the line, this way if one is taken the others will be safe” the old man said, speaking so clinically about the lives of him and his children.

Vic would not allow it as the guard reached him and began to extend his hand to escort Vic out, he reached under his shirt and plucked the smaller dagger from the waistband of his pants. He flipped it so he was holding the blade and with a quick throw sent it spinning towards the other guard. It caught the man’s gun strap on his shoulder and then plowed into the wooden door frame trapping the guard against the wall. In the surprise he reached under to the small of his back and withdrew the larger dagger, pointing it at the bishops throat the tip just mere millimeters away from his jugular Vic stood in front of the man and very quietly spoke. “Now, you will listen to me, you will return my wife and children and allow us to leave this place, if you follow I will kill you regardless of what that means for my soul, don’t test me on this old man, I will do anything to protect my family know this” and the knife pressed against the old man’s throat drawing a drop of blood.

The older priest did not move nor did he look scared, in fact as odd as it was he seemed pleased. “Would you Victor, would you do anything to protect your family?” he asked throwing Vic’s words back at him.

Vic stared oddly at the old man, “What are you getting at priest” he said still with that heat in his voice. The Bishop took two fingers and moved the tip of the knife blade away from his throat, Vic allowed it, with his other hand he waved the guard off as he was about to knock Vic out with the butt of his rifle, of course Vic had not seen this he had been concentrating on the priest in front of him.

“Sit down Victor, have some more coffee” Said the Bishop taking his cup in hand. Victor flopped down in his seat and suddenly had a pretty good idea what the Bishop wanted, him. The Bishop laid it out for him, he would join the order, become a hunter and his family would remain intact and sent elsewhere to live, with new identities and under the protection of the church. They would never know what had happened that night and would be allowed normal lives, the price for this was Victor himself. He would be Declared dead and be the property of the church for as long as he could hunt.

Victor looked down at the dagger in his hands, he knew he had no choice, He had to protect his family and the only way to do that was to hunt that which was coming for them.

He agreed hanging his head, he would never be allowed to see his wife or children again.
